pr_title: Flash.add_flash_types should define helpers as private
pr_body:
Replaces #44868 to fix #44867.

Based on feedback from:
https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/44868#pullrequestreview-1618692109

/cc @r7kamura 

Repro:

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'bundler/inline'

gemfile do
  source 'https://rubygems.org'

  #gem 'rails'
  gem 'rails', path: '~/code/rails'
end

require 'rack/test'
require 'action_controller/railtie'

class TestApp < Rails::Application
  config.root = __dir__
  config.hosts << 'example.org'
  config.session_store :cookie_store, key: 'cookie_store_key'
  config.secret_key_base = 'secret_key_base'

  config.logger = ::Logger.new($stdout)
  ::Rails.logger  = config.logger

  routes.draw do
    get '/notice' => 'test#notice'
  end
end

class TestController < ActionController::Base
  include ::Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

  def notice
    head :ok
  end
end

require 'minitest/autorun'

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  include ::Rack::Test::Methods

  def test_notice_action
    get '/notice'
    assert last_response.ok?
  end

  private

  def app
    ::Rails.application
  end
end

```
pr_comments: I simplified your patch a bit, but LGTM.
Ahh, I was looking for `private :method` but thought it was called something else... :facepalm:

issue_context.title: Actions named `#alert` and `#notice` are not available from Rails 7
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

Run this test:

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'bundler/inline'

gemfile do
  source 'https://rubygems.org'

  gem 'rails', '~> 7.0.0'
end

require 'rack/test'
require 'action_controller/railtie'

class TestApp < Rails::Application
  config.root = __dir__
  config.hosts << 'example.org'
  config.session_store :cookie_store, key: 'cookie_store_key'
  secrets.secret_key_base = 'secret_key_base'

  config.logger = ::Logger.new($stdout)
  ::Rails.logger  = config.logger

  routes.draw do
    get '/notice' => 'test#notice'
  end
end

class TestController < ActionController::Base
  include ::Rails.application.routes.url_helpers

  def notice
    head :ok
  end
end

require 'minitest/autorun'

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  include ::Rack::Test::Methods

  def test_notice_action
    get '/notice'
    assert last_response.ok?
  end

  private

  def app
    ::Rails.application
  end
end
```

### Expected behavior

When I define an action named `#alert` or `#notice`, I expect it to work normally.

### Actual behavior

This test succeeds on Rails 6.1, but fails on Rails 7.0.

comments:
I think this is due to the following change:

- https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/42768

and this problem is also mentioned at https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/42768#issuecomment-1018121461.

A quick fix would be removing `:notice` from the flash_types:
```
class TestController < ActionController::Base
  include ::Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
  self._flash_types -= [:notice]

  def notice
    head :ok
  end
end
```
But `_flash_types` is not public API, so it might be removed or changed in the future.

Another solution could be emitting a warning instead of silently ignoring the method.
We used to do this for `scope` to warn when the named scope overrides an existing
implementation, but that has been removed/added multiple times:
https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/43163#issuecomment-915811613
But silently ignoring a defined method is harder to debug than overriding the
implementation, so it might make sense to add it in this case.

review_comments: How is this not a breaking change?

Hum you are right, I didn't pay attention to the test name, just saw it was testing it wasn't a public method anymore.

Not sure how we could emit a deprecation though. Feel free to revert if you think it's too much of a breaking change.

I don't think the flash methods (alert/notice) are meant to be public, although they definitely were and that _is technically_ a breaking change.

I could only find those methods being documented on the hash itself:
https://edgeapi.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionDispatch/Flash/FlashHash.html#method-i-notice

Based on #33569 and 7265b89, this test is here to ensure the `flash` methods are available even if `helper_method` (via Ac::Helpers`) is not included, like for API only apps. Not to have them be callable directly on the controller's public API, which results in them being treated as actions.

I would append this test with this:

```diff
diff --git a/actionpack/test/controller/flash_test.rb b/actionpack/test/controller/flash_test.rb
index 0ba679684d..c7dbf853a9 100644
--- a/actionpack/test/controller/flash_test.rb
+++ b/actionpack/test/controller/flash_test.rb
@@ -365,7 +365,11 @@ def test_flash_unusable_in_metal_without_helper
       end
     end

-    controller = controller_class.new
+    controller = controller_class.new()
+    controller.request = ActionDispatch::Request.new({})
+
+    assert_respond_to controller.flash, :notice
+    assert_respond_to controller.flash, :alert
```

But that said, you have a point, and I'm open to suggestions on how to handle it (changelog, revert, etc).
I agree with zzak, I think this test is correct now.
